title: Variables
summary: Named containers that store values. In Luau you almost always create them with `local` — bare assignments create globals, which is usually a mistake.

syntax: local name = value      -- preferred: local variable

details.heading: Naming rules
details.body: Names must start with a letter or underscore, then contain letters, digits, or underscores. Names are case-sensitive (`Score` and `score` are different). Reserved words like `local`, `function`, `end`, `if`, `true`, `nil` cannot be used as names.

details.heading: Globals
details.body: Assigning to a name that was never declared `local` writes to the global environment `_G`. This is legal but slow, typo-prone (a misspelled name silently creates a new global instead of erroring), and forbidden by most Roblox linters (Luau-LSP, Selene).

explanation.whatItIs: A variable is a name that refers to a value, so you can store something once and use it many times. Think of it as a labeled box: `local coins = 50` labels a box with the number 50, and every time you write `coins` Luau hands you whatever is in that box right now.
explanation.whyItExists: Without variables you would have to recompute and retype every value constantly, and you could not track state that changes over time (health, coins, whether a door is open).
whenToUse: Whenever you need to remember a value for later: `local playerName = player.Name`
To give a meaningful name to a long expression: `local spawnPoint = workspace.SpawnLocation.Position`
To hold state that changes: `local score = 0` … `score = score + 10`
whenNotToUse: Don't create globals by forgetting `local` — always write `local` unless you have a specific reason not to
Don't create a variable you only use once if the expression is already clear — `print(player.Name)` needs no intermediate variable
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
local coins = 50        -- label "coins" now points to 50
coins = coins + 10      -- read 50, add 10, point "coins" at 60
print(coins)            --> 60
```
A variable is a *label on a value*, not the value itself. Reassigning moves the label.
tips: Use descriptive camelCase names: `playerHealth`, not `ph` or `x`
Declare variables as close to where they're used as possible
commonMistakes: Forgetting `local`, which creates a global: `score = 0` instead of `local score = 0`
Misspelling a name and silently creating a second variable: `playerScore` vs `playerScor`
Confusing `=` (assignment) with `==` (comparison). `if x = 5` is a syntax error

examples.title: Creating and updating a variable
examples.code:
local coins = 50
print(coins)        --> 50

coins = coins + 25  -- update it
print(coins)        --> 75
examples.whyItWorks: `local coins = 50` creates the variable. `coins = coins + 25` reads the current value (50), adds 25, and reassigns the name to the new value (75).

examples.title: Variables hold any type of value
examples.code:
local playerName = "Raanis"      -- string
local health = 100                -- number
local isAlive = true              -- boolean
local inventory = {}              -- table
local target = nil                -- explicitly "nothing"

print(playerName, health, isAlive)
examples.whyItWorks: A variable can hold any Luau value. Unlike some languages, Luau variables are not locked to one type — but in Roblox code it is still good habit to keep each variable's type consistent.
